Who is signed in, and what they may do

Source: R/rights.R
soil_whoami.Rd

Reads the identity of the session from its access token, without any request: user name, subject, the rights (Keycloak client roles of the API audience, e.g. soil:read), what they allow, the limits advertised by the server and how long the session lasts.

Usage

soil_whoami(soil = soil_session())

Arguments

soil

A session from soil_connect(); the default session when omitted. Client-side: not sent to the API.

Value

A soil_identity list: username, subject, audience, roles (character), rights_known, can (named logical: summary, read, publish, admin; NA when the rights are not declared in the token), limits (the limits of /capabilities, advertised by the server for this deployment, NULL when not read), token_expires_at, session_expires_at (expiry of the refresh token, NA when unknown), session_renewable, last_renewed_at, renewals and status ("signed_in" or "expired").

Details

The API has no identity endpoint: rights are read from the token payload (resource_access[[audience]]$roles), as the API reads them; the audience comes from soil_connect()'s reading of /capabilities (authentication.audience, soil-api). When the token has no resource_access entry for the audience (no block at all, or a block without the audience, as with rights granted by a policy decision point) the rights are "not declared in the token; the API decides" (can is NA), and no local check is made before a request.

Rights and functions:

  • soil:summary – discovery and catalog, summaries, availability, consistency;

  • soil:read – observations, features, values, health scores, exports;

  • soil:publish – runs, publications, source ingest, jobs;

  • soil:admin – variables, products, versions, country refresh.

See also

soil_connect(), soil_session()

Other session: soil_connect(), soil_login(), soil_logout(), soil_session()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
soil <- soil_connect()
me <- soil_whoami(soil)
me$can
me$token_expires_at
} # }
